transfers.source_mechanism: Flow-dependent structural modification in myxomycete networks
transfers.target_problem: A mid-sized city (population 800,000) has a traffic signal network with 247 signalized intersections. The current signal timing plan is optimized centrally every 6 months using a macroscopic traffic model, but it cannot adapt to real-time conditions: incidents, weather, special events, and construction. Re-optimizing centrally every minute is computationally infeasible and would require expensive predictive models. The city wants a distributed, adaptive signal timing approach that uses only local traffic flow measurements (vehicle count and queue length at each intersection) to adjust green-split and offset in real time, without a central optimizer.
transfers.transferred_principle: Flow-dependent feedback enables adaptive network optimization through local structural modifications
transfers.required_translation: Replace biological material flow with traffic flow, pressure differentials with traffic congestion differentials, and structural reinforcement/atrophy with signal timing adjustments. The myxomycete's cytoplasmic streaming becomes vehicle movement, while the protoplasmic tubes become traffic lanes. The feedback gain regime translates to a proportional control system that adjusts signal timing based on local queue length and vehicle count measurements.
transfers.expected_effect: Each intersection adjusts its signal timing based on local traffic conditions and neighboring intersection states, creating a self-optimizing traffic network that adapts to real-time conditions without central coordination
boundary_conditions: Each intersection has only local traffic measurements (count and queue length)
transfers.testable_prediction: When implementing this distributed adaptive signal system, the average vehicle delay at intersections will decrease by at least 15% compared to the current 6-month-optimized static plan during non-incident conditions, and by at least 30% during incident conditions, while maintaining convergence within 15 minutes of any perturbation.
